_about: Words that the backward pass writes without the circumflex that a later norm added. Each list holds the rows of one backward edge, and no forward pass reads it. The 1911 and 1943 norms write the differential circumflex (êste, sôbre), and so does the table of the 1971 reform, which is also the backward map from br_1971 and ao1990-br. Pre-1911 print writes the bare form, and the 1913 print in the 1911 spelling writes toda, todo and fez bare. No orthographic norm governs pre-1911 print, so usage decides: each row quotes the counts of the bare and accented form. The list for reforma_1911 holds the words that the 1913 print writes bare. The list for etymological holds those words and the ones that the 1913 print still accents, which pre-1911 print writes bare. côr keeps its circumflex (côr 310, cor 5 in the 13 books; 12 of 13 write the accent more often), pôde stays as the table gives it, and the contraction pelo and the preposition por are bare in every norm, so neither has a row.
